changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/plugin-detail-8937-parent-scope-residue.md`

- names `RelatedList.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - **`packages/plugin-detail/README.md` (it is in `files[]`, so it ships).** It said the node's `filter` is AND-combined with `{ [relationshipField]: parentId }`, full stop. Since objectui#7299 the parent condition is compiled to match the relationship field's arity, so a multi-valued relationship gets `{ [relationshipField]: { $contains: parentId } }` instead. The paragraph now states both spellings and names the arbiter (`@objectstack/spec/data`'s `isMultiValueField`). - **The claim that the SQL driver decides arity on that same predicate.** It does not: `driver-sql` gates the equality family on its own storage question, which reads `multiple` as truthy on ANY type. The two rules therefore disagree for a type outside `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` carrying `multiple: true`. objectui#9184 moved the arity compiler into `@object-ui/core`'s `parent-scope` seam and carried the claim with it, so the correction is recorded there — the seam now states the driver's measured rule, records the divergence as a divergence, and points at the upstream card that owns which of the two rules is right (objectstack#17469). `RelatedList.tsx`'s pointer comment and the objectui#7299 test header carried the same sentence and are corrected to match.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `f9d772b16` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1540 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2126 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36186183509)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `977c4c69309e57aba342fddbb4d61d79c9000ca1`

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card objectui#10690 (body and all three comments), the cited objectui#7299 thread (triage 5548394236, dispatch 5606992805, dev report 5607739381), the objectui#8882 body, PR 10718's body, file list and check-runs, the diff at merge-base `383a34f529f6c60d3da4c1b76b502635f89a8b8d` against head `977c4c69` (4 files, +208/−112, fetched into `refs/review/pr-10718`), `packages/react/src/hooks/useSettledSchema.ts` at head, the ObjectMap and ObjectDataTable gates on `refs/review/main`, AGENTS.md (#10, #11, 版本号策略, the changeset-presence rule) and `.changeset/config.json`. The os-dev-report's claims were not used as evidence; every line below was checked against the diff.

Binding text, triage `5837899985` execution note: 「gate `RelatedList`'s fetch on `useSettledSchema(api, dataSource)`, as `object-map` and `object-data-table` do in PR objectui#10688. Flip the DECLARED COST pin to a one-read pin with `$contains` on the first read, and keep its `SINGLE_VALUED` control.」 The claim `5837949980` limits the surface to `RelatedList.tsx` (its own record fetch and the child-definition read that feeds it), the 7299 pin, and one changeset; not `DetailView.tsx`, not the picker's definition read, not the lookup hydration, no run-guard or `error` lifecycle change, no new published prop.

Behaviour, accepted-set and surface changes, item by item (file:line at the head):

1. The gate — RIGHT. `packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx:534` replaces the local `useState` fed by its own effect (base :513 and :855–861) with `const { ready: objectSchemaReady, def: objectSchema } = useSettledSchema(api ?? '', dataSource)`: the same key the base read with (`getObjectSchema(api)`) and the same trigger set (`api`, `dataSource`). The fetch effect (:933) returns at `:976` (`if (!objectSchemaReady) return;`) immediately after `setLoading(true)` at `:968`, inside the `api && !dataProvided` branch (:950). That is the sibling placement: `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectDataTable.tsx:775–779` and `packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx:862–865` both hold the placeholder and return while not ready, inside the branch that queries. The exits that precede the gate, `filterRefusal` (:942–945) and `!canScope` (:954–967, the "refusing to fetch all rows" guard objectui#7299 forbade weakening), are untouched; the `dataProvided` path never reaches the gate.

2. Dependency list — RIGHT. `:1141` gains exactly one entry, `objectSchemaReady`, a boolean. The definition object is not named: it reaches the query only through `referenceFieldIsMultiValue` (:884–887, a memo whose value is a boolean), `expandKey` (:732) and `selectKey` (:861), all compared by value. This is stricter than the siblings, which also name `objectSchema` itself (ObjectMap :1058, ObjectDataTable :789). AGENTS.md #10 holds. An `api` switch: the hook derives `ready = resolution !== null && resolution.key === key` at render time (`useSettledSchema.ts:220`), so the new `api` reads not-ready in the very render it changes; the effect re-runs on `api`, stops at the gate, and fetches only after the new definition settles. It cannot borrow the previous object's definition; pinned by `SWITCH` (7299 pin :467–492: the multi-valued child receives only the `$contains` query, the earlier single-valued object only its equality one). Residual worth naming, not a defect and not the brief's case: a `dataSource` identity switch with the SAME `api` keeps `ready` true across the hook's refetch (the hook's documented design, identical in both siblings), so that re-run can query with the previous adapter's definition and run again if a content key then moves; the base did the same with no gate at all.

3. Stranding — none, in source and in pins. Hook `useSettledSchema.ts:198–204`: `!dataSource || !settleKey || typeof dataSource.getObjectSchema !== 'function'` calls `settle(null)` before any `await` in `resolve()`, so the no-source case settles synchronously inside the hook's first effect run and issues no definition read; `:208–211` settles `null` on a thrown read (after `console.error`). `ready` therefore becomes true in every case and `referenceFieldIsMultiValue` stays `false` on a `null` def, so the list fetches with the equality form. Pins: `SETTLES — no getObjectSchema` (7299 pin :433–445) reads `find`'s call count as 1 with no `await` after `render()`, then the rows; `SETTLES — a definition read that throws` (:447–465); the unchanged `COUNTER-PROBE — no schema at all` (:387–396) still demands one equality read. The literal `dataSource` undefined branch is the same `if` and is pinned at the hook (`useSettledSchema.test.ts:32`, :48, :76). Confidence-gap answer verified: with no `getObjectSchema` the first paint waits for no definition read, only one extra render; with `getObjectSchema` present the row query now follows the definition read instead of running beside it, which is the cost the adjudication accepted and the PR body states.

4. Run guards and forbidden regions — unchanged. `let cancelled = false` (:937), `if (cancelled) return;` (:1021, :1098), `if (!cancelled) setLoading(false)` (:1048, :1107) and the cleanup `cancelled = true` (:1110–1112) sit outside all nine hunks. The picker's own definition read (:895–906) and the lookup hydration (:1194–1276) are byte-identical to the base (region-diffed). `DetailView.tsx` is not in the file list. The component has no `error` state to move. No prop, type or export changes anywhere in the diff.

5. Logging — inside the claim. Base :855–861 (`console.warn('[RelatedList] Failed to fetch schema for …')`) is deleted with the effect it lived in; the hook reports the same failure at `console.error` (`useSettledSchema.ts:209`). The claim's surface names "the child-definition read that feeds it", and that read is precisely what was replaced, so its reporting moves with it. No component state, prop or export moves; the changeset states the change.

6. Raw-URL fallback — a follow-on behaviour change, RIGHT. With a schema-only adapter (has `getObjectSchema`, no `find`), a multi-valued relationship now reaches the refusal arm (:1065–1090) with the arity known and sends no request, where the base sent the equality URL once and then refused. Pinned as `[]` (7299 pin :515–534). With no adapter at all the arity is unknowable and the equality URL still goes out, as before; the raw-URL `CONTROL` (:536–544) is unchanged.

7. Doc comments rewritten in `RelatedList.tsx` (:513–533, :723–731, :783–785, :795–799, :853–859, :876–884, :969–975, :1130–1140): each now states the gate and the settle-on-every-exit property; checked against the hook, every sentence is true. They cite by symbol and test name, never by a cross-file `path:line` (AGENTS.md #11).

Asked and missing: nothing. Gate on `useSettledSchema(api, dataSource)` ✓. `DECLARED COST` flipped to `ONE READ`, whose first and only query is the `$contains` form ✓ (7299 pin :284–301). `SINGLE_VALUED` control kept, assertion unchanged, only its comment reworded ✓ (:303–313). One changeset, `patch` for `@object-ui/plugin-detail` ✓.

Done but not asked:
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.relatedBadgeArity-8882.test.tsx`, outside the claim's declared surface. Judged on the brief's three questions. (a) It is a second pin of the SAME decision: its old case text says verbatim 「`RelatedList` refuses to gate rows on a loaded schema … so it attempts equality, is refused, and refetches」 and asserted `rowQueries().length` greater than 1 with equality first (base :392–415); the adjudication reverses exactly that decision. (b) The flip is load-bearing: on the fix `rowQueries()` holds exactly one entry, so the old `waitFor` could never resolve and the Test shards would be red; the new case `ONE READ EACH` (head :391–412) asserts rows exactly `[{ $contains }]` and badge probes exactly `[{ $contains }]`, stricter than before on both sides. No guard weakened. (c) The badge-arity assertion the file exists for (objectui#8882: same `$filter` on both reads) is asserted unchanged: `SUBJECT — the badge probe sends the SAME parent condition as the rows` (:372–389, byte-equal `$filter`), `SUBJECT — badge/row parity at a POSITIVE count` (:414–430) and `LIVE CONTROL` (:432–445) are untouched; only the `renderAndCollect` comment (:310–315) and the one case moved, and `renderAndCollect` still fails loudly if either read never happens (:293–297). Test-only, same vitest and type-check family, no release surface. Acceptable; the seat owes the claim record the added path.
- Three cases added to the declared pin file (`SETTLES` twice, `SWITCH`) and a `listElement` helper for the rerender: they pin the adjudication's own safety argument and the confidence gap. Within the work of flipping the pin.

Existing pins edited: (i) `DECLARED COST` → `ONE READ`: was two reads with equality first, now exactly one read carrying `$contains`, read after the rows render plus a settle window. Strengthens, and is red on the base by construction (the base sends equality then `$contains`). (ii) Raw-URL refusal: was exactly one equality URL, now none. Strengthens; red on the base. (iii) 8882 `MEASURED DIFFERENCE` → `ONE READ EACH`: above. No pin was deleted and no guard weakened.

New pins can fail: negative leg — `ONE READ`, `SWITCH` and the raw-URL case each assert a call list that on the base contains the extra equality attempt; the evaluator `matchOne` (7299 pin :154–183) throws `INVALID_FILTER` on equality over an array and `evaluate` (:186–196) refuses empty or unsupported filters, so a wrong spelling cannot pass as "no rows". The `SETTLES` cases fail against a gate that waits for a definition rather than a settle (call count 0, no rows). Lit control — `CONTROL — a single-valued relationship keeps bare equality, byte for byte` (green in both worlds, unchanged), the raw-URL `CONTROL` (unchanged) and `COUNTER-PROBE — no schema at all` (unchanged).

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/10690-related-list-reads-once.md`: `'@object-ui/plugin-detail': patch`. Against AGENTS.md 版本号策略: no `major` (mandatory, CI-enforced) ✓; breaking changes would be `minor`, and there are none: no prop, export, type or accepted-payload shape moves, so `patch` is the right level for a behaviour fix on a published component. Both `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/app-shell` are in the `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, so one entry bumps the whole family; the app-shell edit is a test file that publishes nothing and needs no entry of its own (`scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` header: an added changeset satisfies the gate, and empty frontmatter is the form for a test-only PR, which this PR is not). Not a `content/docs/**` change; the diff adds no docs or README prose. The plugin-detail README sentence at :460 ("once the child schema has loaded, the fields the row predicates read") stays true.

Changeset prose, sentence by sentence:
1. "A related list reads its rows once per mount, after its child object's definition settles, so a multi-valued relationship's first query is already the `$contains` membership form (objectui#10690, auto-adjudicated B by triage)." — TRUE for the definition-driven reads (gate :976; `ONE READ`).
